observations.content: Assistant updated APTIS/inventory-tai-lieu.md replacing the unresolved rar entry with a full inventory of 99 extracted files (24 docx, 37 doc, 35 pdf) in the aptis writing folder, resolving the blocked rar entry.

Assistant found 3 most valuable items in the 99 writing files: graded real B2 test with examiner feedback (Helen_writing_test_SK_Serian_B2_with_commentsrev.docx), an exaggerated formal letter paired with an informal message to teach register duality, and the stencil method PPTX matching the frame bank philosophy.
Assistant told user everything is ready for Day 1; only unreadable items left are old .ppt binaries and 52 audio files user must listen to.
User exported 11 Aptis Writing Overview.ppt to PDF and asked what remains to be done.

Assistant read 11 Aptis Writing Overview.pdf (14 pages, titled PowerPoint Presentation, author Allford, Scott (Malaysia)) and identified it as a British Council training presentation containing CEFR A0-C writing descriptors and per-part assessment criteria.

Assistant found the PDF's pages 7-10 contain stock phrases for formal emails: lead-in phrases, final-sentence stock phrases, sign-off phrases (formal vs informal), and how to make questions relevant and polite.
Assistant updated inventory replacing the deprecated .ppt entry with the new PDF entry and noted the .ppt original can be ignored.

Assistant confirmed nothing text-based remains unreadable; only 52 audio files (including mẹo aptis.mp3 29MB, skipped as official tips already available) remain, and duplicate zips in mat/ are left as-is.
User said 'Ok bắt đầu đi' to begin Day 1.

Assistant extracted the authentic Part 4 prompt from Helen's docx: annual fundraiser dinner 'Education for All' cancelled due to lack of support; task A write ~50-word email to a friend (10 minutes) with feelings and alternative suggestions, task B write 120-150-word email to club secretary (20 minutes).
Quiz 1 (answered correctly): Overall CEFR in Aptis = rounded average of the 4 skill CEFR levels; user's L(C) R(C) S(B1) W(C) gives Overall C; 174/200 total does not decide CEFR.

Quiz 2 (answered correctly): Core Grammar & Vocabulary has no own CEFR but bumps a skill sitting just below a threshold (grey area, ~1 measurement error) up a band; user's R44 and W46 were below the C threshold (46/48) yet still got C due to G/V 40.

Assistant taught Writing format: 50 minutes, 4 parts sharing one scenario; Part 1 five very short replies (band 0-3, ~3min), Part 2 20-30 words (band 0-5, ~7min), Part 3 three social media replies 30-40 words each (~10min), Part 4 two emails (informal 40-50 + formal 120-150 words, band 0-6, ~30min, the only band ordering to B2.1/B2.2/C1/C2).
Quiz 3 (answered correctly): correct time strategy is to do the first three parts fast and keep ~30 minutes for Part 4, treating early parts as cheap points.

Assistant taught register duality: register is chosen by reader (friend=informal, club secretary=formal), not by politeness level; B2 barem requires correct register in both emails or cap blocked at B1.

Assistant taught frame bank method: memorizing a whole script scores 0, but memorizing the frame (open/intro/feelings/suggest/ask/close/sign slots) and slotting in the task content is valid; gave a 5-slot formal Part 4 frame template.

Assistant noted Helen's B2 model answer naturally used a conditional ('If we could postpone it to December, maybe we could...') matching the user's studied type 2 conditional, showing grammar and register combine in one email.

Quiz 4: user selected 'I don't know' (said they were leaning toward answer 4 but not certain), correct answer was 'I was deeply disappointed to learn of this.' as the formal equivalent of 'I'm really gutted about this'; formal phrases must be non-contracted, objective, no exclamations.
